feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 0 (0.6 kg, baseline geometry) is the only stable design, with the oval at 20/20 in 1.65 s, oscillation 0.15 and score 356.6, and iteration 9 reproduced it. Mass has never been tested alone at baseline geometry. Iteration 1 (0.5 kg with a 0.10 m track, 0.033 m radius and wide array) and iteration 2 (0.5 kg with the wide array) both lost oval finishes and raised oscillation to 0.26 and 0.21, but iteration 7 showed the wide array alone collapses the oval at 0.6 kg, so the 0.5 kg effect is confounded. For the controller I kept the iteration-0 baseline exactly, so the mass is the only variable. Interpret the next race as follows. If the oval holds at 20/20 near 1.65 s and oscillation falls below 0.15, mass is damping the controller and a small further increase is worth testing. If the oval falls below 20/20 or oscillation rises above about 0.2, mass is an oval-sensitive axis and the 0.6 kg baseline should be the final geometry. If the bends stay near progress 0.17 (s-bend) and 0.12 (slalom) under any geometry, the bend limit is probably controller-side and should not be chased with further geometry changes.
requested_changes: If the oval holds at 20/20 near 1.65 s and steering_oscillation falls below 0.15, test mass 0.8 kg alone at baseline geometry and controller, to see whether damping keeps improving or starts to cost the oval finish.
If the oval falls below 20/20 or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, return to mass 0.6 kg and treat the iteration-0 platform as the final geometry, since mass is the oval-sensitive axis.

Keep sensor_positions at x = +/-0.024 m with y = 0.05 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.12 m and wheel_radius 0.03 m for the next test. Iterations 3 to 8 show each of these collapses the oval when changed alone, so the bends should not be pursued through them.
